preamble: Substitution of the voiced bilabial stop [b] for the voiceless labiodental fricative [f] is attested in early Latin loanwords in Basque. Basque had no native /f/, and early borrowings with initial [f] were received as [p] or [b] depending on the dialect (Latin festa > besta ~ pesta, fortis > bortitz). Word-initially Basque had no contrast between voiced and voiceless stops, which favoured the [b] outcome.

examples.note: Early loans with initial [f] were taken in as [b] or [p] depending on the dialect, not as [h].

sources: Wikipedia. Influences on the Spanish language (Latin f > h and Basque). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Influences_on_the_Spanish_language
